common_name: South Pacific Scarlet Canna (AAS-Winning Seed-Grown Canna)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes or seed-grown transplants once soil has warmed; South Pacific Scarlet was an All-America Selections winner bred to flower reliably from seed in a single season, producing vivid scarlet-red blooms on compact, uniform plants with attractive green foliage.

directions: Plant rhizomes or seed-grown transplants a few inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun. South Pacific Scarlet was recognized as an All-America Selections winner for its ability to flower reliably and uniformly from seed within a single growing season, an important breakthrough for a genus traditionally propagated by rhizome division, which made cannas slower and more expensive to bring to market as bedding plants. It produces vivid, true-scarlet flowers on compact, well-branched plants with clean green foliage, blooming continuously from early summer through frost. Like other cannas it is a heavy feeder needing consistent moisture and excellent drainage to avoid rhizome rot, and it overwinters reliably in the ground in zone 9 and warmer, forming an expanding clump over time. In colder zones, lift rhizomes after the first killing frost and store them dry over winter.
sources: All-America Selections — South Pacific Scarlet Canna Award Notes

common_name: Cannova Canna (Compact Weather-Tolerant Seed Canna Series)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes or seed-grown transplants once soil has warmed; Cannova is a compact, seed-grown canna series bred for improved wind and rain tolerance compared to older tall canna cultivars, staying tidy and upright through summer storms.

directions: Plant rhizomes or seed-grown transplants a few inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun. Cannova is a modern canna series bred for a more compact, weather-resistant habit than older, taller canna cultivars, with sturdy stems that hold up better to wind and heavy rain, an important trait during Gulf Coast summer storms that can flatten taller, top-heavy cannas. The series is available in a range of flower colors including scarlet, gold, rose, apricot, and bronze, all on clean green foliage, blooming continuously from early summer through frost. Like other cannas it is a heavy feeder needing consistent moisture and excellent drainage to avoid rhizome rot, and it overwinters reliably in the ground in zone 9 and warmer, forming an expanding clump over time. In colder zones, lift rhizomes after the first killing frost and store them dry over winter.

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring and plant in rich, moist, well-drained soil once soil has warmed; Intrigue is grown primarily for its narrow, dark purple-bronze foliage, an unusual fine-textured leaf form quite different from the broad paddle-shaped leaves of most canna cultivars.

directions: Plant rhizomes a few inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun. Intrigue is grown chiefly for its distinctive, narrow, deeply colored purple-bronze foliage, a finer-textured leaf shape than the broad, paddle-like leaves typical of most canna cultivars, giving it an almost banana-leaf-meets-grass appearance that stands out in a tropical-themed border. Smaller orange flowers appear above the foliage in summer, though the striking leaf color and texture remain the plant's primary ornamental draw. Like other cannas it is a heavy feeder needing consistent moisture and excellent drainage to avoid rhizome rot, and it overwinters reliably in the ground in zone 9 and warmer, forming an expanding clump that benefits from periodic division. In colder zones, lift rhizomes after the first killing frost and store them dry over winter.

common_name: Pretoria Canna (Yellow-Green Striped Foliage Orange Canna)

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring and plant in rich, moist, well-drained soil once soil has warmed; Pretoria is a classic large-leaved canna cultivar with bold yellow-and-green striped foliage and vivid orange flowers, one of the longest-cultivated striped-leaf canna varieties.

directions: Plant rhizomes a few inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun. Pretoria is a classic, long-cultivated canna prized for large, bold, paddle-shaped leaves striped lengthwise in bright yellow and green, topped with vivid orange summer flowers, similar in overall effect to the more recently introduced Bengal Tiger but with a somewhat larger, more substantial leaf. Its bold tropical foliage makes it a striking specimen or focal point even when not in bloom, useful for anchoring a tropical-themed border or providing a backdrop for smaller plants. Like other cannas it is a heavy feeder needing consistent moisture and excellent drainage to avoid rhizome rot, and it overwinters reliably in the ground in zone 9 and warmer, forming an expanding clump that benefits from periodic division. In colder zones, lift rhizomes after the first killing frost and store them dry over winter.

planting.note: Divide rhizomes in early spring and plant in rich, moist, well-drained soil once soil has warmed; Wyoming is a classic large canna cultivar with dark bronze-purple foliage and bright orange flowers, a long-standing favorite for tropical-style borders.

directions: Plant rhizomes a few inches deep in rich, consistently moist, well-amended soil in full sun. Wyoming is a classic, long-cultivated canna bearing large, deep bronze-purple leaves that provide dramatic dark color and bold tropical texture through the growing season, topped with bright, true-orange flowers that stand out sharply against the dark foliage. Its substantial size and strong color contrast make it a favorite anchor plant for tropical-themed borders and mixed plantings alongside cannas of contrasting leaf color. Like other cannas it is a heavy feeder needing consistent moisture and excellent drainage to avoid rhizome rot, and it overwinters reliably in the ground in zone 9 and warmer, forming an expanding clump that benefits from periodic division. In colder zones, lift rhizomes after the first killing frost and store them dry over winter.
